title: Microsoft Teams: third-party synthetic audio and video detection in meetings
summary: The briefing's controls, opt-in behaviour and rollout dates are supported. Its cost rating describes indirect costs only despite documenting separately licensed provider services; the unpublished provider price does not make that licensing requirement disappear. Microsoft's two setup references also use different names for the provider application identifier.

claims.claim: Third-party detection is admin-opt-in and does not start in existing meetings without provider configuration.
claims.quote: For third-party detection, use only the Teams App ID of a supported certified detection provider and set SyntheticMediaDetection to Enabled.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting protection > Synthetic audio and video detection provider > Turn on synthetic audio and video protection reaches the detection setting.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select an existing meeting policy ... Under Meeting protection, select a provider from the Synthetic audio and video detection provider dropdown list. ... The Turn on synthetic audio and video protection setting appears

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy-name> -SyntheticMediaDetection Enabled -SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId <supported-provider-app-id> selects a provider using its Teams App ID.
claims.quote: Replace <supported-provider-app-id> with the Teams App ID of a supported certified detection provider, not an arbitrary Microsoft Entra application ID or bot ID.
claims.fix: Keep the call and add this sentence to controls[0].note: "The cmdlet reference specifies the provider's Teams App ID, whereas the feature overview's PowerShell example labels it 'provider bot application ID'." The differing example is at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout and After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the app's tenant status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <value> updates an app's tenant state through a Boolean parameter.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... -IsBlocked ... The state of the app in the tenant. ... Type: Boolean

claims.claim: App availability, consent, provider activation and meeting policy configuration are separate prerequisites, and blocking the app controls the integration rather than the meeting setting.
claims.quote: A provider appearing in the list doesn't mean that app availability, admin consent, or provider-side activation is complete. ... App availability and required consent must remain in place for the integration to function.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes -IsBlocked $true as unblocking an app.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Learn describes the feature and its admin setup route as public preview.
claims.quote: This feature is currently in public preview. ... You can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to turn on synthetic audio and video detection in a meeting policy.

claims.claim: Public-preview detection results use the provider's experience.
claims.quote: In public preview, detection results are surfaced through the provider's experience.

claims.claim: Native Teams detection alerts, participant indicators and associated actions are separately in private preview.
claims.quote: Native Teams detection alerts, participant indicators, and associated actions are available separately in private preview.

claims.claim: UI labels and supported scenarios can change before general availability.
claims.quote: Features, user interface labels, and supported scenarios can change before general availability.

claims.claim: The Graph beta reportSyntheticMedia action lets an admitted certified detection bot flag a participant.
claims.quote: This action is intended for certified third-party audio and video synthetic media detection bots admitted to the meeting call. The detection bot calls this action to flag a participant whose stream it identifies as AI-generated or synthetic media.

claims.claim: The Graph reference says detection results propagate to all participants through roster updates.
claims.quote: The detection result is propagated to all participants via roster updates.

claims.claim: Reality Defender RealMeeting has a Microsoft 365 App Certification programme page.
claims.quote: # Reality Defender RealMeeting ... Publisher Attestation: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer

claims.claim: Pindrop Pulse has a Microsoft 365 App Certification programme page.
claims.quote: # Pindrop Pulse ... Certification information ... APPLICATION SECURITY ... PASS

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to review provider terms, data handling and compliance documentation before enabling detection.
claims.quote: Certified third-party providers may analyze meeting audio/video signals for synthetic media detection. Review provider terms, data handling, and compliance documentation before enabling.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's attested page lists the Calls.AccessMedia.All application permission.
claims.quote: Calls.AccessMedia.All | application

claims.claim: Reality Defender's permission justification states access to real-time meeting audio and video for authenticity analysis.
claims.quote: The app is a meeting-recording bot, so it needs Graph to join Teams meetings and access the real-time audio and video media in order to run authenticity and deepfake analysis.

claims.claim: The Reality Defender page is based on the developer's own self-assessment.
claims.quote: The information on this page is based on a self-assessment report provided by the app developer on the security, compliance, and data handling practices followed by this app.

claims.claim: Microsoft makes no guarantee of the accuracy of that self-assessment.
claims.quote: Microsoft makes no guarantees regarding the accuracy of the information.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents contains details of synthetic media detection events in Teams.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents table in the advanced hunting schema contains details about synthetic media (deepfake) detection events in Microsoft Teams in your organization.

claims.claim: The hunting table is populated from Defender for Office 365 records.
claims.quote: This advanced hunting table is populated by records from Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: The table contains data only when an approved detection engine is used.
claims.quote: This table contains data only if you're using an approved detection engine: Microsoft or a third-party engine (GetReal, Pindrop, Reality Defender, or Resemble AI).

claims.claim: Synthetic media detection hunting is a Microsoft 365 E5 or Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 capability.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5 and Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 extend Teams protection ... Hunting on synthetic media (deepfake) detections in Teams: You can hunt for synthetic media (deepfake) detected in Microsoft Teams using the SyntheticMediaDetectionEvents advanced hunting table.

claims.claim: The hunting table names detected users.
claims.quote: DetectedUserDisplayName | string | Display name of the user flagged as using synthetic media

claims.claim: The hunting table names meetings.
claims.quote: SourceContextName | string | Name of the source (for example, the meeting, file, or email name)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance controls
claims.claim: The tenant administrator must grant the app Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission before a third-party bot can report detections.
claims.quote: Third-party bots can invoke this action only when the meeting tenant administrator grants the app the Calls.ReportSyntheticMedia.All application permission.

claims.claim: Saving a meeting policy does not establish that the App ID identifies a supported detection provider.
claims.quote: Successfully saving the policy does not guarantee that the App ID identifies a supported provider or that the detection bot can join meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can stop the bot joining eligible meetings.
claims.quote: An incorrect or unsupported App ID can prevent the detection bot from joining eligible meetings.

claims.claim: In private preview, the organizer can remove a flagged participant from the alert or roster.
claims.quote: This experience is available only in private preview. ... From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: Remove the flagged participant from the meeting.

claims.claim: In private preview, the organizer can select Mark as not a concern from the alert or roster.
claims.quote: From the alert or the roster, the organizer can: ... Mark as not a concern to dismiss the alert when the organizer has verified the participant.

claims.claim: Teams does not automatically remove detected participants.
claims.quote: Teams doesn't remove participants automatically. The organizer decides what action to take.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can rescan a participant.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: Reality Defender's publisher-attested listing says hosts can end the meeting if manipulation is detected.
claims.quote: Hosts can rescan a participant or end the meeting if manipulation is detected.

claims.claim: Detection is the provider's assessment rather than verified proof of manipulation.
claims.quote: Detection (verdict) ... The provider's assessment that a specific participant's audio, video, or both appear to be synthetic or manipulated. ... Certification doesn't validate the accuracy of a provider's detection models.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.claim: Users receive the global meeting policy unless a custom policy is created and assigned.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: The feature page requires Teams Administrator or higher to manage the app and meeting policies.
claims.quote: You have the Teams Administrator role (or higher) to manage the app and meeting policies.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Users and policies; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting SyntheticMediaDetection to Disabled turns detection off for meetings organized by users assigned that policy, regardless of provider.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "SyntheticDetectionPolicy" -SyntheticMediaDetection Disabled ... disables synthetic audio/video detection for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, regardless of the configured detection provider.

claims.claim: Disabling detection leaves SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId unchanged.
claims.quote: The SyntheticMediaDetectionAppId value is unchanged.

claims.claim: SyntheticMediaDetection defaults to Enabled, which permits detection when a configured provider is available.
claims.quote: Enabled: Permits synthetic media detection when a configured detection provider is available. This is the default value.

claims.claim: The default App ID is the zero GUID and does not select a third-party provider.
claims.quote: The default value, the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000), selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available. It does not select a third-party provider.

claims.claim: The App ID parameter documentation refers to Microsoft Detection when available.
claims.quote: selects no provider when Microsoft Detection is unavailable, or Microsoft Detection when it is available.

claims.claim: Cost is low because the cost the sources show is administrator time, although the page also documents provider add-on licensing.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; licensing: model: "add-on"; "Complete any provider-side licensing or service activation before setup"; "the cost the sources show is administrator time."
claims.fix: Set cost to medium under the standard's add-on licensing scale. Replace the cost rationale with: "Medium. Detection requires a provider service under its own licensing and activation model. Microsoft has not published provider fees or a detection-specific Teams licence, price or meter." The published licensing prerequisite is at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/third-party-synthetic-audio-video-detection-meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[0].note; Scope: Users and policies; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Provider selection is per meeting policy and applies to meetings organized by users assigned that policy.
claims.quote: updates an existing meeting policy to permit synthetic audio/video detection using a configured third-party provider for meetings organized by users assigned this policy, when the feature and provider are available.

claims.claim: Detection providers are independent vendors with their own terms.
claims.quote: Detection provider ... An independent software vendor (ISV) ... Processing, retention, and residency of that media are governed by the provider's terms and privacy statement.

claims.claim: Some provider apps require publisher configuration before an administrator allows them.
claims.quote: Before an admin allows an agent or app, it shows as Blocked by publisher in the admin center. Before you allow it for users, follow the publisher's guidance to configure it.
